title: POC Weekly - Redwood Private VPC Pilot Sync
summary: Weekly check-in on Redwood Private VPC pilot: networking and routing progress, kernel/agent upgrade schedule, initial perf/latency numbers after KV cache tuning, next steps for security reviews and a short downtime window for upgrade. SE and customer engineers aligned on test plan; security to review KMS/keys and audit log config.
topics: Routing and egress (transit gateway vs NAT)
Initial benchmark results: latency and p50/p95
KV/prefix cache tuning and batching improvements
next_steps: Redwood to share upgraded install runbook and downtime window proposal (Ava) by 2025-12-12
Customer to validate firewall rules and confirm egress IPs (Tom) by 2025-12-13
Marcus to run targeted p95 latency benchmark after KV cache tuning and post-upgrade and share results (Marcus) by 2025-12-17
Evelyn to review KMS/HSM integration doc and confirm any extra requirements by 2025-12-15
Schedule final production cutover planning call the week of 2025-12-22
action_items: Ava Chen - send upgraded install runbook + proposed downtime window - due 2025-12-12
Tom Gallagher - confirm VPC peering and provide required egress IPs - due 2025-12-13
Marcus Lee - run p95/p99 latency benchmark after tuning and provide CSV + grafana links - due 2025-12-17
Evelyn Park - review KMS/HSM integration notes and list missing compliance items - due 2025-12-15

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-12-10
Time: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Ava Chen (Redwood AE), Marcus Lee (Redwood SE), Jorge Ramos (Redwood CSM); Priya Desai (SignalPath Head of ML), Tom Gallagher (Infra), Evelyn Park (Security), Nate O'Connor (SRE)

[00:00] Ava Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'll kick us off. Quick agenda — networking/routing status, kernel/agent upgrades, perf review from Marcus, security questions, and next steps. Anything to add?

[00:18] Priya Desai: No that's good. Wanted to make sure we cover the KV cache tuning results; we ran some of Marcus's suggestions yesterday.

[00:30] Marcus Lee: Great. I'll walk through the numbers. Quick note — some of the names in the config got munged in the earlier doc, so watch for the agent id that ends with -02, that's the one we patched.

[00:45] Tom Gallagher: Sorry, quick callout on networking — we still have the intermittent failure on the cross-account VPC peering at the transit gateway level. It's not constant but it spikes during larger batches.

[01:05] Marcus Lee: Right, that matches the batching pattern. When the prefix cache warms, we see improved latency but the bursts are creating TCP churn. We're recommending adding explicit route propagation and bumping the MTU on the TGW attachments.

[01:30] Nate O'Connor: We're a bit nervous about changing MTU in prod; we need a test window. Also need confirmation on the egress IPs so our outbound rules don't block the agent telemetry.

[01:55] Ava Chen: Understood. Tom, can you confirm the list of egress IPs today? We sent a spreadsheet but I don't know if you received the final list.

[02:05] Tom Gallagher: I have the spreadsheet but the CIDR for the east region was different — I need the canonical list. I'll confirm by EOD.

[02:22] Marcus Lee: On the perf numbers — after KV prefix caching adjustments and increasing max batch window to 40ms, p50 dropped from 38ms to 29ms, p95 from 210ms to ~160ms in our synthetic tests. p99 still a bit high at 520ms; we traced that to cold KV misses and a couple of long-tail kernel preemption events.

[02:50] Priya Desai: That's promising. Is that with the current private deployment or a mix?

[02:56] Marcus Lee: Those numbers are from the private VPC pilot cluster, on the 4-GPU nodes you have provisioned. We did disable quantization fallback for the test; it's a straightfp run to isolate scheduling effects.

[03:20] Evelyn Park: From a security standpoint, we need to confirm KMS key rotation policies and whether Redwood's control plane ever stores plaintext keys or ARNs. We have to show this to compliance for SOC2.

[03:40] Jorge Ramos: Quick clar — Redwood Private has customer-managed KMS; the control plane stores only key ARNs and never plaintext. We do have audit logs for key usage that can be shipped to your SIEM.

[03:55] Evelyn Park: Right, but we need a sample of those audit logs with PII redaction to show the auditors. Also SSO — is SAML mapping for groups available?

[04:12] Ava Chen: Yes, SAML SSO and SCIM for group sync are supported; we'll attach the SSO mapping doc post call.

[04:25] Priya Desai: Great. Back to kernel upgrades — Marcus, you mentioned a kernel bump to 0.9.4-rc yesterday? Concern about downtime?

[04:35] Marcus Lee: Yep. The rc includes two fixes: much better memory reclamation during long sequences and a fix to the attention cache invalidation in some edge cases. We expect a short rolling restart per node — around 6-8 mins per node if we do a rolling upgrade.

[04:50] Tom Gallagher: That rolling restart is fine but we need a formal downtime window and a plan for warmup traffic. The pilot cluster is still on our staging traffic pattern.

[05:05] Ava Chen: Proposal: run the upgrades in a 4-hour maintenance window during low traffic — we'll cordon nodes, drain, upgrade agent, and run a smoke workload. Marcus will do post-upgrade benchmark and Nate will watch alerts.

[05:20] Nate O'Connor: We need clear rollback steps if p95 regresses. Can you share the rollback playbook?

[05:28] Marcus Lee: Absolutely — rollback is just redeploying previous agent and rolling the node back, but we'll capture snapshots of the model state and KV caches before restart to accelerate warmup. I'll include exact commands in the runbook.

[05:45] Priya Desai: About the KV cache — we observed that after a node reboot the first 300-400 tokens are slow because the prefix cache is cold. Is there a recommended warmup sequence or prepopulate?

[06:02] Marcus Lee: Two options — pre-warm via replay of representative request set (preferred) or snapshot the prefix/KV cache and restore, but the latter has consistency concerns if you have multi-node writes. For this pilot, replaying a sample set (we'll provide a small harness) is lowest risk.

[06:25] Tom Gallagher: Ok we'll take the harness. Also, what's the impact on billing during the upgrade? We want to ensure we don't get charged for double-running nodes unintentionally.

[06:40] Jorge Ramos: For Dedicated/Private billing we bill on provisioned capacity; short-term double-running during upgrade is usually minimal but we'll flag the upgrade window as non-billing-affecting where possible. We'll confirm the exact cost delta.

[06:55] Evelyn Park: Back to audit logs — where do they reside? Can we push logs directly to our S3 or to Splunk?

[07:05] Marcus Lee: We can ship logs via Kinesis or forward to S3; we also support pushing to your Splunk HTTP endpoint with basic signing headers. We'll add the sample config.

[07:22] Priya Desai: Any issues with model weights integrity during upgrade? We use a 3rd-party model variant — the onboarding had a small mismatch earlier where manifest names were different.

[07:35] Marcus Lee: We saw that — the manifest mismatch was due to the model bundle naming convention. We pushed a fix to the loader to tolerate the alias. That should be fine now, but we'll include the exact model manifest we used in the runbook.

[07:55] Tom Gallagher: One more networking nuance — when we route egress through the transit gateway the TLS session times out at 15 minutes and that causes persistent connections to drop under long-live requests. Any suggestions?

[08:10] Marcus Lee: We recommend keeping the connections shorter and use connection pooling at the application layer; also check the idle timeout on the TGW and bump it if possible. We have a connection-keepalive helper in the SDK.

[08:28] Priya Desai: On the perf front — Marcus, could you share the raw traces for the p99 spikes? We want to correlate with our app logs.

[08:35] Marcus Lee: Sure — I'll upload the trace snippets and a sample flame graph. Some of the p99 spikes map to KV cold misses and one to kernel GC scheduling. That's the low-level kernel preemption I mentioned.

[08:48] Priya Desai: Do you think quantization could reduce p99? We haven't tried the int8 variant in the private cluster yet.

[08:55] Marcus Lee: Quantization will reduce average latency and CPU usage but can increase variance if there's fallback to fp in certain ops. For p99, the biggest wins are warm cache and reduced GC, but int8 helps p50/p95 mostly. We can run a controlled int8 test in staging.

[09:12] Evelyn Park: Can we get a security checklist for the private control plane? Items like where logs are stored, role-based access, KMS key ownership, SSO mapping, and network egress.

[09:22] Ava Chen: Yes — we'll attach the security checklist; Marcus will also include examples of audit logs and the KMS flow.

[09:34] Tom Gallagher: About the agent upgrade, what's the exact version and are there breaking changes? We don't want surprises to the inference API.

[09:42] Marcus Lee: Version 0.9.4-rc has no API contract changes — only runtime fixes and a small CLI flag rename (agent.startup.timeout -> agent.start_timeout). We'll call out that rename in the runbook.

[09:55] Priya Desai: Good. For the telemetry, do you keep any sample payloads? We need to ensure no customer data is in logs.

[10:05] Jorge Ramos: We sample telemetry but PII is redacted by default; we can provide a sanitized sample set for your auditors.

[10:18] Nate O'Connor: Metrics thresholds — what thresholds should we set for alerts during upgrade? CPU at 85%? p95 > 400ms?

[10:28] Marcus Lee: Reasonable starting points: CPU > 80% for 2 minutes, p95 > 350ms, error rate spike > 0.5%. We'll share a Grafana dashboard template you can import.

[10:40] Priya Desai: Anything else before we wrap?

[10:45] Tom Gallagher: I'll confirm the egress IPs and send back firewall rules by EOD.

[10:50] Ava Chen: Great. To recap: Ava will send runbook + proposed downtime window by Friday 12/12; Marcus will run post-upgrade benchmarks and upload traces by 12/17; Evelyn will review KMS notes by 12/15; Tom will confirm egress CIDRs by EOD today. We'll schedule the final cutover planning call week of 12/22.

[11:10] Priya Desai: Thanks all. Appreciate the concrete plan.

[11:15] Ava Chen: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up in email and link the docs. Bye.

[11:20] (meeting ends)

Notes about transcription: occasional speaker attribution errors and minor mis-hearings (e.g., TGW vs "transit wig" in one auto-generated line). Some long sentences have been left unedited to preserve natural cadence.
